title: Damron-Hanson-Houdre-Xu (2019) prove ANTI-CONCENTRATION rather than a variance lower bound: for GENERAL edge-weight distributions on Z^d they show T(0,x) is with high probability not contained in an interval of size o(log||x||)^{1/2}, with similar statements for first-passage percolation in thin cylinders. In the same abstract they record that the log||x|| variance lower bound was found in the 1990s and 'there has not been any improvement since'.
body:
general i.i.d. edge-weight distributions on Z^d - the point of the paper is removing the special-distribution restriction under which such statements were previously proved
the conclusion is anti-concentration (an interval-avoidance statement), NOT a variance lower bound
the log||x|| variance lower bound it cites is available only in two dimensions

WHY THE DISTINCTION IS NOT PEDANTRY: an anti-concentration statement bounds how much mass the law of T(0,x) can put in a short interval. It does not by itself lower-bound the variance, and a variance lower bound does not by itself give anti-concentration. Chaining them silently is a category error.
METHOD: inducing a fluctuation in the number of edges in a box whose weights are of 'hi-mode' (large).
THE LITERATURE STATEMENT IS THE SECOND REASON THIS NODE EXISTS: it is a dated, first-hand confirmation from four people working directly on the problem that Newman-Piza's logarithmic bound had not been improved.
SOURCE: arXiv:1810.08270v2, 'Lower bounds for fluctuations in first-passage percolation for general distributions'. Official arXiv API record retrieved by lane P4 on 2026-08-22.
VERIFICATION STATUS: theorem-checked-against-source at abstract level for both the conclusion shape and the literature statement; the proof was not read and the precise 'general distributions' hypothesis is not stated in the abstract.
